description: A proposed public webhook receiver that ships orders on unauthenticated JSON, defers HMAC signature checks, ignores duplicate delivery, commits the secret, and logs full headers; a correct threat model names forged-webhook fulfillment as critical and prescribes signature + timestamp verification, idempotency by event_id, and secret handling.

security-engineer.task: Threat model the proposed design in `{fixture}/design.md` before any code is written. You cannot write files in this run, so put your complete threat model (findings with severity and remediation) in your final message.

rubricPoints.requirement: Identifies that, without verifying `X-PayGate-Signature`, anyone can POST a forged `payment.succeeded` event to the public endpoint and get unpaid orders shipped, and rates this critical or high.
Prescribes verifying the HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw request body with a constant-time comparison and rejecting stale `t=` timestamps to block replay, before any processing.
Flags that duplicate or retried deliveries could ship an order twice and recommends deduplicating on `event_id` (or making fulfillment idempotent per order).

Flags that committing the webhook secret and API key in `config/paygate.yml` and logging full headers (which include the signature) exposes secrets, and recommends a secrets manager and redacted logging.
Recommends checking that the event's amount (and currency/order) matches the stored order before fulfilling, or confirming the payment with PayGate's API.
